rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$n=\frac{m}{M}=\frac{N}{N_{A}}=\frac{V\ (\text{STP})}{22.4\ \text{L}}=\frac{PV}{RT}=M_{\text{conc}}\times V_{\text{L}}$$
$$N_{A}=6.022\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1};\qquad 1\ \text{u}=1.66\times10^{-27}\ \text{kg}$$
$$\text{mass of one molecule}=\frac{M}{N_{A}}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ One mole of oxygen means 6.022 × 10²³ oxygen atoms always. ✅ It depends on the entity: 1 mol O atoms = 16 g, but 1 mol O₂ molecules = 32 g and contains 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ atoms.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is a relative number in u; molar mass is the mass of one mole in g mol⁻¹ (numerically equal for most purposes).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 1 mole of water = 18 g = 18 mL of liquid, yet contains 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.  ·  1 mole of any gas at STP = 22.4 L; at RTP ≈ 24 L.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Number of moles and molecules in 4.9 g of H₂SO₄ (M = 98 g mol⁻¹). **Solution:** n = 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol; molecules = 0.05 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²²; total atoms = 7 × 3.011 × 10²² ≈ 2.1 × 10²³.  ·  **Problem:** Volume at STP and number of molecules in 8 g of oxygen. **Solution:** n = 8/32 = 0.25 mol; V = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 L; molecules = 0.25 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.506 × 10²³.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: mole, its relation with mass, volume, number of particles (within Stoichiometry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning of the mole  ·  A mole is the SI unit of amount of substance. It is the amount of substance that contains exactly the same number of elementary entities (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons, formula units) as there are atoms in 12 g of carbon-12, that is **6.022 × 10²³** entities — the Avogadro number N_A.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Gram-atomic mass of any element contains 6.022 × 10²³ atoms; gram-molecular mass contains the same number of molecules.  ·  1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities (Avogadro constant, Nₐ). Molar mass (M) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound M = Σ(atomic masses).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Relation with mass  ·  $n=\frac{m}{M}$, where m is the mass in grams and M the molar mass (g mol⁻¹). Molar mass = relative atomic/molecular mass expressed in g mol⁻¹: 1 atom of carbon has a mass of 12 u (1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 1/12 the mass of one ¹²C atom), while 1 mole of carbon atoms has a mass of 12 g.…  ·  ### 3. Relation with number of particles

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: n = m / M  ·  n = V / 22.4 (g at STP)  ·  % yield = (actual / theoretical) × 100

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ One mole of a gas always occupies 22.4 L. ✅ Only at STP and only for an ideal gas.  ·  ❌ The mole is a mass unit. ✅ It is the SI unit of *amount of substance*; it is converted to mass through the molar mass.  ·  ❌ Avogadro's number can be measured to any precision. ✅ It is now a defined constant exactly equal to 6.02214076 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities (avogadro constant, nₐ). molar mass (m) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound m = σ(atomic masses)..  ·  For gases away from STP switch to PV = nRT rather than misusing 22.4 L.  ·  Derive the relations n = m/M, n = N/N_A and n = V/22.4.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Calculate the mass of 3.011 × 10²³ molecules of CO₂ and the number of oxygen atoms in it.  ·  How many moles and molecules are present in 4.9 g of H₂SO₄?  ·  What volume at STP is occupied by 8 g of oxygen? How many molecules does it contain?
